# ArkType

> TypeScript's 1:1 validator, optimized from editor to runtime

ArkType parses definitions written in TypeScript's own syntax, validates data against them at runtime and infers their types. ArkRegex, Attest and @ark/json-schema are its companion packages.

Each link below is a docs page as Markdown. [llms-full.txt](https://arktype.io/llms-full.txt) has every ArkType page in one file.

## ArkType: Get started

- [Setup](https://arktype.io/docs/intro/setup.md): Install ArkType and configure TypeScript to infer your types correctly.
- [Your first type](https://arktype.io/docs/intro/your-first-type.md): Define a type with TypeScript syntax, compose it, and validate data with it.
- [Adding constraints](https://arktype.io/docs/intro/adding-constraints.md): Narrow types beyond what TypeScript can express, with keywords, ranges, divisors and custom predicates.
- [Morphs](https://arktype.io/docs/intro/morphs-and-more.md): Transform data as part of validation by piping it through functions and other Types.
- [Cheat sheet](https://arktype.io/docs/cheat-sheet.md): ArkType's most common syntax, patterns and gotchas on one page.
- [Agents](https://arktype.io/docs/agents.md): Help Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other coding agents write ArkType.
- [Editor setup](https://arktype.io/docs/editor.md): Highlighting, inline errors and autocomplete for ArkType definitions in VS Code, JetBrains IDEs and other editors.

## ArkType: Definitions

- [Primitives](https://arktype.io/docs/primitives.md): Define strings, numbers, bigints, symbols, booleans, null and undefined, with literals, patterns, lengths, ranges and divisors.
- [Objects](https://arktype.io/docs/objects.md): Define objects, arrays, tuples, dates and class instances, and derive new object types from existing ones.
- [Keywords](https://arktype.io/docs/keywords.md): Every built-in keyword, from TypeScript's own types to subtypes like string.email and generics like Pick.
- [Expressions](https://arktype.io/docs/expressions.md): Combine, refine, transform and annotate types with operators like unions, intersections, narrows, pipes, brands and metadata.
- [Match](https://arktype.io/docs/match.md): Branch on the type of a value with ArkType definitions, like a type-safe switch statement.
- [Scopes](https://arktype.io/docs/scopes.md): Define aliases that reference each other, then use them in definitions or export them as a module of Types.
- [Generics](https://arktype.io/docs/generics.md): Declare definitions with parameters and instantiate them like TypeScript generics.
- [Declare](https://arktype.io/docs/declare.md): Define a Type that must match an existing TypeScript type exactly.

## ArkType: Validation

- [Validation](https://arktype.io/docs/validation.md): Check data against a Type by calling it, asserting it or testing it with allows.
- [Errors](https://arktype.io/docs/errors.md): Read, serialize and throw the errors a Type returns for invalid data.
- [Traversal API](https://arktype.io/docs/traversal-api.md): The ctx argument that narrow and pipe functions receive for reading the current path and reporting errors.

## ArkType: Configure

- [Configuration](https://arktype.io/docs/configuration.md): Change ArkType's defaults and error messages globally, for a scope or for a single Type.
- [i18n](https://arktype.io/docs/i18n.md): Write ArkType's error messages in another language, per app or per request.

## ArkType: Interop

- [Standard Schema](https://arktype.io/docs/standard-schema.md): Pass a Type to any library that accepts a Standard Schema, and use other validators inside an ArkType definition.
- [Integrations](https://arktype.io/docs/integrations.md): Use a Type directly with tRPC, oRPC, Drizzle, React Hook Form, Hono, the MCP SDK and the AI SDK.
- [fast-check](https://arktype.io/docs/fast-check.md): Generate test data from a Type for property-based tests with @ark/fast-check.
- [Ecosystem](https://arktype.io/docs/ecosystem.md): Community projects built on ArkType, for environment variables, Drizzle codegen and binary serialization.

## ArkType: Reference

- [Type API](https://arktype.io/docs/type-api.md): Every member of a Type and of the type function.
- [Packages](https://arktype.io/docs/packages.md): Every package ArkType publishes, its entrypoints, and what to import from each.
- [Upgrading](https://arktype.io/docs/upgrading.md): The changes in the latest ArkType that can break code written for the previous release, and what to change.
- [FAQ](https://arktype.io/docs/faq.md): Answers to common questions about ArkType's behavior, configuration and TypeScript integration.

## ArkRegex

- [Overview](https://arktype.io/docs/regex.md): Install ArkRegex and see what it infers from the strings you already pass to new RegExp().
- [Inference](https://arktype.io/docs/regex/inference.md): The type ArkRegex infers for each part of a regular expression.
- [Errors](https://arktype.io/docs/regex/errors.md): Which mistakes in an expression are type errors, and which aren't checked.
- [Types](https://arktype.io/docs/regex/types.md): The Regex type and its members, plus regex.infer, regex.parse, regex.validate and regex.as.
- [ArkType](https://arktype.io/docs/regex/arktype.md): How ArkType infers its regex literals and accepts regex() values as definitions.
- [FAQ](https://arktype.io/docs/regex/faq.md): Why some expressions infer string or fail to infer, and the cases ArkRegex currently gets wrong.

## Attest

- [Getting started](https://arktype.io/docs/attest.md): Install attest and run its setup and teardown around your tests.
- [Assertions](https://arktype.io/docs/attest/assertions.md): Assert on types, values, errors, completions, JSDoc and type instantiations from any test runner.
- [Benches](https://arktype.io/docs/attest/benches.md): Measure the type instantiations and runtime of a block of code against a baseline stored inline.
- [Options](https://arktype.io/docs/attest/options.md): Every attest option, its default, and how to set it from setup, a flag or an environment variable.
- [CLI](https://arktype.io/docs/attest/cli.md): Summarize, trace and precache your project's type performance from the attest command.
- [Custom assertions](https://arktype.io/docs/attest/integration.md): Read the type data attest collects from your own assertion functions.

## JSON Schema

- [Overview](https://arktype.io/docs/json-schema.md): Generate JSON Schema from a Type with arktype, or build a Type from JSON Schema with @ark/json-schema.
- [To JSON Schema](https://arktype.io/docs/json-schema/to-json-schema.md): Generate a JSON Schema from any Type, pick a draft, and decide what to write for what JSON Schema can't express.
- [From JSON Schema](https://arktype.io/docs/json-schema/from-json-schema.md): Parse a JSON Schema into a Type with @ark/json-schema and give the result a static type.
- [Keyword support](https://arktype.io/docs/json-schema/support.md): Which JSON Schema keywords @ark/json-schema converts, which throw, and which it ignores.

## Internals

- [Architecture](https://arktype.io/docs/internals.md): How ArkType is split into @ark/util, @ark/schema, arksets and arktype, and what each package owns.
- [Nodes](https://arktype.io/docs/internals/nodes.md): The node kinds every Type is built from, and how to read them with .internal, .json and select.
- [Schemas](https://arktype.io/docs/internals/schemas.md): Build Types from @ark/schema's object format with type.schema, rootSchema, node and schemaScope.
- [Set algebra](https://arktype.io/docs/internals/sets.md): What importing arksets installs into @ark/schema, and what @ark/schema does without it.
